title: How the buddy falls asleep
intro: You said you didn't love the shut-down pose as written. A is that pose, as close as the app can get to it, so the other two are judged against the thing you're reacting to. Every pane runs the whole thing on a loop — he settles, breathes while he's under, and wakes — because two thirds of a sleep pose is motion and a picture can only show the middle of it. "Wake him" triggers the wake on demand. They're at his real size: 112 pixels, the same as the window he actually lives in. The theme buttons at the top right re-run all three in another theme.

steps.headline: Which way of falling asleep reads best?

variants.label: Loaf
variants.summary: The film's own pose. He squats down and his arms swing under to the bottom corners. Watch whether you read those as tucked arms or as short legs — that ambiguity is my main worry with it.

variants.label: Slump
variants.summary: Dozed off where he stood: he leans, sinks a little, his arms go slack. His outline barely changes, so nothing has to be worked out — but it's also the closest to how he already looks when idle.

variants.label: Dim
variants.summary: Shrinks a touch, settles, and fades to about half brightness. The only one that says 'powered down' through brightness rather than posture — so it's the one that still works when he's small, or docked half-off a screen edge.

steps.headline: Should little z's drift up off him while he sleeps?
steps.changed: Whichever posture you picked above, small z's can rise and fade above his head while he's under.
steps.notice: It removes all doubt about what he's doing — nobody has to work out his posture to know he's asleep. It is also the one part of this that isn't him: it's a bit of cartoon furniture floating in the corner of your screen.
steps.risk: Motion. A sleeping buddy is supposed to be the quiet state, and z's keep something moving forever — which is exactly what you asked the ambient tier NOT to do when there's a status light that needs to stand out.
